title: fix(app-shell): the bell's approvals link and app paths key on the route segment (objectui#11818)
body:
Fixes #11818

Clause-②: no. No export, prop, route or `packages/i18n` key changes. One published option, `UseTrackRouteAsRecentOptions.appName`, gets a corrected JSDoc and no type change. The hook has always compared that value against the URL's app segment, so the doc now says it is the route segment, and this repo's only caller now passes that.

## What changed

ADR-0048 option A keys `/apps/SEGMENT` on the package id and keeps the app name only as a fallback alias (`utils/appRoute.ts`). `ConsoleLayout` publishes the app's **name** as `currentAppName`, which matches that field's declared contract ("Current app name"). The defect is in consumers that splice that name into a path.

- **`layout/InboxPopover.tsx`, `goToApprovals`: the triage pin.** It built the path from `currentAppName ?? params.appName` raw, so the name won over the route's segment. It now reads `hostAppSegment`. That is the `resolveHostAppSegment` result the two "View all" drills and the notification-row link in the same file already use, hoisted above the handler.
  - From `/apps/com.example.showcase/…`, *View approvals* now lands on `/apps/com.example.showcase/system/approvals`.
  - On `/home` (the bell outside `/apps/APP/*`), it opens the remembered app by its package id if that app is still active, and otherwise the first active app. Before, it went to `setup`. This is the answer Home's approvals card already gives.
- **`console/AppContent.tsx`, recent-items tracker.** It handed `useTrackRouteAsRecent` `activeApp.name`. The hook records a route only when the pathname's app segment equals that value. So on a package-id route, which is the address every sidebar link builds, no object, dashboard, page or report visit was recorded. AppContent now resolves one `appSegment`: `appName` (the URL's own segment), else `appRouteSegment(activeApp)`. The tracker and the four `activeApp.name` path fallbacks in the same file now build on it.
- **`views/global-search-renderer.tsx`, outside the app router.** The block fell back to `currentAppName` raw. With nothing remembered, the segment was empty and the rendered link collapsed to `/apps/OBJECT/record/ID`, with the object's name where the app belongs (measured in the ablation below). It now uses `resolveHostAppSegment(apps, currentAppName)`. Inside the router the URL's own segment is kept.

## Every app-scoped link site in `packages/app-shell/src`, with its verdict

Population: every non-test `/apps/${…}` template in `packages/app-shell/src` on `cef0eee` (`git grep -n '/apps/\${'`), plus the `useTrackRouteAsRecent` caller and `homePath.ts`. A concatenated spelling (`'/apps/' +`) was searched for too and has no hits. Sites are named by file and quoted expression, not by line.

| File | Expression | Value is | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layout/InboxPopover.tsx` | `goToApprovals`: `currentAppName ?? params.appName` | app **name** first | **defect, fixed** |
| `layout/InboxPopover.tsx` | drills and notification row: `hostAppSegment` | resolved segment | correct |
| `console/AppContent.tsx` | `useTrackRouteAsRecent({ appName: activeApp?.name })` | app **name** | **defect (live), fixed** |
| `console/AppContent.tsx` | package-metadata redirect `appName ?? activeApp.name`; `handleRecordFormSuccess` and `handleEdit` `baseUrl` name fallback; `metadata/package/*` Navigate `appName ?? activeApp.name` | route param, then **name** | **defect (dormant), fixed**. The console mounts AppContent only under `/apps/:appName/*`, so these fallbacks are unreachable there. They are fixed because they are in the same file and the edit is mechanical. |
| `console/AppContent.tsx` | `DraftReviewNavigator`, `navigate_create` / `navigate_edit` `defaultBaseUrl`, create-first-app CTA | route param | correct |
| `console/AppContent.tsx` | `handleAppChange(newAppName)` | callers (`AppSwitcher`, `CommandPalette`) pass `appRouteSegment(app) ?? app.name` | correct |
| `console/AppContent.tsx` | `ConsoleLayout activeAppName={activeApp.name}` | the name, per `currentAppName`'s declared contract | not a link; unchanged (producer) |
| `views/global-search-renderer.tsx` | `appName \|\| currentAppName \|\| ''` | route param, then **name** or empty | **defect, fixed** |
| `hooks/useTrackRouteAsRecent.ts` | `href` built on its `appName` option | whatever the caller hands it | correct once the caller passes the segment; JSDoc corrected |
| `chrome/CommandPalette.tsx` (held by objectui#11812, not edited) | `appName \|\| appRouteSegment(activeApp)`; app switch `appRouteSegment(app) ?? app.name` | route param, then segment | correct: no name-first site there |
| `console/ConsoleShell.tsx` | `appRouteSegment(setupApp) ?? SETUP_APP_PACKAGE_ID` | segment | correct |
| `console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx` | `open_record` hand-off: fetched `_packageId`, else `setup`; `onOpenBuiltApp`: `appSegment ?? appName` | package id / segment first | correct |
| `console/ai/LiveCanvas.tsx` | `routeSeg = appSegment \|\| appName` | segment first | correct |
| `console/home/AppCard.tsx`, `console/home/HomePage.tsx` (four) | `appRouteSegment(app) ?? app.name`, `hostAppSegment` | segment | correct |
| `console/marketplace/*` (six files) | `useParams().appName` | route param | correct |
| `hooks/useInboxArrivalNotifier.ts` | `hostAppSegment` | resolved segment | correct |
| `hooks/useObjectActions.ts` | `useParams().appName` | route param | correct |
| `layout/AppHeader.tsx` | breadcrumb `appNameFromRoute`; help docs `currentAppPackageId`; app list `appRouteSegment(app) ?? app.name` | route / package id / segment | correct |
| `layout/UnifiedSidebar.tsx` | `appRouteSegment(activeApp)` | segment | correct |
| `utils/appRoute.ts` | `resolveNotificationTarget` host | resolved segment | correct |
| `utils/homePath.ts` | `resolveDeclaredHomePath`: `/apps/${declared.name}` | **name**, by documented design | **not fixed**: see Acceptance notes |
| `views/InterfaceListPage.tsx`, `views/PageView.tsx` (via `pageRecordActions.ts`) | pathname segment | route | correct |
| `views/ObjectDataPage.tsx`, `views/ObjectView.tsx`, `views/RecordDetailView.tsx` (four), `views/RecordFormPage.tsx`, `views/RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx`, `views/SearchResultsPage.tsx`, `views/useOpenRecordList.ts` | `useParams().appName` | route param | correct |
| `views/app-launcher-renderer.tsx`, `views/nav-menu-renderer.tsx` | `appRouteSegment(…) ?? …name` | segment | correct |
| `views/metadata-admin/QuickFind.tsx` | `appSlug` prop, else relative `..` | host-supplied; no in-repo caller passes one | correct |
| `views/metadata-admin/ResourceListPage.tsx`, `previews/ToolPreview.tsx` | `useParams().appName` | route param | correct |
| `views/metadata-admin/previews/AppPreview.tsx`, `inspectors/AppNavInspector.tsx` | nav-preview hrefs, "Open" link, landing preview on the app's metadata `name` | **name** (designer preview) | **not fixed**: see Acceptance notes |

## Reverse verification

Each fix was committed first, then reverted on disk through `node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. That tool requires its anchor to hit once, checks the blob hash before and after, and proves the restore with blob equal to `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`. I wrote down the expected direction before each run. All three runs matched it.

- **`goToApprovals`** reverted to `currentAppName ?? params.appName`: `Tests 5 failed | 2 passed (7)`. The triage pin received `"/apps/showcase_app/system/approvals"`, the URL the card reports. The `/home` cold landing received `"/apps/setup/system/approvals"`. Both controls stayed green: an app with no package id, and the URL segment alone.
- **The tracker input** reverted to `activeApp?.name`: `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2)`. The package-id route recorded nothing (expected 1 entry, received 0). The name-alias control stayed green.
- **`global:search`** reverted to `appName || currentAppName || ''`: `Tests 2 failed | 2 passed (4)`. The two outside-router cases received `"/apps/showcase_app/showcase_task/record/T1"` and `"/apps/showcase_task/record/T1"`. The two in-router controls stayed green.

## Gates (HEAD `d4235cd`, after the last commit)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over 27 files, run under the container verify lock. The files are every `InboxPopover.*`, every `AppContent.*`, `useTrackRouteAsRecent.test.tsx`, `global-*.tsx` in `views/__tests__`, `HomePage.approvalsTarget.test.tsx` and `AppHeader.inboxVariant.test.tsx`. Result: `Test Files  27 passed (27)`, `Tests  247 passed (247)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/app-shell^..." build`, then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`. The type-check echoed `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. `BUILD_EXIT=0` and `TC_EXIT=0`. The test project's `include` glob covers the three new test files; I did not count them with `--listFiles`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, `✅  7 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: exit 0, `✅  No changeset declares a major bump.`
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: exit 0, `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0, `✅  check-control-bytes: OK`.
- `pnpm check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`: each exit 0 with its own `✅`/`OK` line.
- ESLint, narrowed to the files this branch changed: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on the 7 lintable changed files gives exit 0 with `0 errors, 46 warnings`. The `--format json` count is 7 files and 0 errors. All warnings are in pre-existing code or copy the sibling test's mock pattern (`no-explicit-any`).
  - Why the narrowing is sound: `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` run belongs to CI.

## Acceptance notes

Not fixed here, with the reason for each:

- **The `/` landing and the logo's home path stay on the name.**
  - `apps/console`'s `resolveLandingPath` returns `/apps/${defaultApp.name}` (and `/apps/${visible[0].name}` for a one-app deployment). `utils/homePath.ts`'s `resolveDeclaredHomePath` returns the same, on purpose: its doc says "The segment is the app's `name` — byte-identical to what `/` has been redirecting to".
  - `landingHomeParity-7256.test.ts` pins the two together. Moving either one alone breaks that pin, and `apps/console` is outside this claim's file surface.
  - Reach: only a deployment that declares an `isDefault` app, or has exactly one visible non-Setup app. The showcase QA environment is neither, and I measured no live door.
- **Designer previews.**
  - `AppPreview`'s nav-preview hrefs and its "Open" link, and `AppNavInspector`'s landing preview, build on the app's metadata `name`. The running sidebar builds on the package id, so the preview shows the alias form.
  - Fixing this needs the package id threaded into `MetadataPreviewProps`, which is a prop change this claim rules out. The alias resolves.
- **`plugin-designer`'s `EditAppPage`** navigates to `/apps/${draft.name}` after a save. For an app that has a package id, that is the alias. This is outside `packages/app-shell` and its reach was not measured. `CreateAppPage` does the same, but correctly: a DB-authored app has no package id, so its name is its segment.
- **The bell inside a hidden app** (`hidden: true`): the approvals link now opens the first active app, as the "View all" drills already did, because `resolveHostAppSegment` re-checks against active, non-hidden apps.
- **Stale prose.** `HomePage.approvalsTarget.test.tsx`'s header still describes the popover's old `currentAppName ?? params.appName` expression. `InboxPopover.viewAllTarget.test.tsx` has one case that sets `currentAppName` to a package id, which the console never publishes. I edited neither because both files are outside this claim.
- **Narrowing I declared.** The first run of the touched test files (8 files, `--maxWorkers=1`) and the three ablations ran outside the verify lock. Before that, the lock queue went about 23 minutes without progress behind a full `packages/app-shell/` and `apps/console/` vitest run. The final 27-file run and the build and type-check above did run under the lock.
